metadata.description: Ringleader Azure onboarding: the OPTIONAL network landing pad (vnet + workstations subnet + NAT gateway + NSG). Deploy at RESOURCE GROUP scope, after azuredeploy.json. Separate from azuredeploy.json on purpose: that file is also deployed by the Terraform module, which compares Azure's normalized echo of it against the file on every plan, so it may carry no outputs block and no parameter default it does not pass. This template is deployed only by az, so it is free to have both.
Prefix for the created resources (vnet, NSG, NAT gateway, public IP). Change it if those names are already taken in this resource group.
Region for the landing pad. Defaults to the resource group's.

A single CIDR allowed inbound on TCP 22. Empty (the default) adds NO inbound rule, which leaves workstations unreachable from outside the VNet -- correct only if you reach it privately (VPN / ExpressRoute / peering). Ringleader ships no bastion and no SSH tunnel: rl shell, tmux, port-forwards and VS Code Web all dial the workstation on 22.

Optional, and empty opens nothing. A single CIDR allowed inbound on the secondary SSH port (TCP 2222). Some Ringleader workstation types run their own SSH daemon on that port inside the VM, beside the VM's own sshd on 22, and rl shell dials it instead of 22 for those; others never use it. An NSG covers the whole subnet, so this admits the port to every VM on it.

Reserve an empty subnet for the DNS / HTTPS proxy VM that Ringleader's hostname-level egress control will use. On by default. The VM is not built yet; carving the range now means the NSG rules that permit workstation -> proxy traffic can name one stable prefix, and avoids renumbering later. It shares the NAT gateway, so the proxy gets egress without a public IP. Azure does not bill for a subnet, so leaving it on costs nothing.
Prefix for the gateway subnet. Must sit inside vnetCidr, and the default sits well clear of the workstations subnet so growing that one later does not collide.

Reserve a second subnet -- the one you put the WORKSTATIONS a gateway governs in. On by default. A gateway steers a whole subnet and serves only the boxes it holds a policy for, so a steered subnet must hold governed boxes and nothing else; the workstations subnet is where every workstation in the VNet goes, governed or not. It carries the same NSG as the workstations subnet, so rl shell still reaches a box in it, and NEITHER a route table NOR the NAT gateway: Ringleader claims the subnet by putting its own UDR on it and declines one that already references a route table, and a governed box's egress is meant to be its gateway's. Azure does not bill for a subnet.

Prefix for the governed subnet. Must sit inside vnetCidr; the default sits immediately below gatewaySubnetCidr at the top of the VNet, so the two egress-control ranges stay together and the workstations prefix is free to grow.

variables.effectiveSubnets: [concat(variables('workstationSubnets'), if(parameters('createGatewaySubnet'), variables('gatewaySubnets'), createArray()), if(parameters('createGovernedSubnet'), variables('governedSubnets'), createArray()))]

metadata.description: The subnet for the workstations a gateway governs, or empty if createGovernedSubnet was false. Hand it back as providerConfig.azure.subnetId on the workstations that carry an egress policy.
The subnet reserved for the future DNS / HTTPS proxy VM, or empty if createGatewaySubnet was false.
